title: Ten years, 31 moments
lede: From the announcement to a forwarded web address. Filter by thread.

events.title: Turner announces FilmStruck
events.text: A subscription service from Turner Classic Movies with the Criterion Collection, due in the fall. Criterion will leave Hulu for it.

events.title: Prices and a date
events.text: Launch is set for October 19: $6.99 a month, $10.99 with the Criterion Channel, $99 a year. Criterion posts a three-minute introduction video the same day.

events.title: The launch is postponed
events.text: The day before the planned opening, Turner delays it to November to finish the sign-up process.

events.title: AT&T agrees to buy Time Warner
events.text: The date of the merger agreement, as given in AT&T’s later filing.

events.title: FilmStruck opens
events.text: United States only, with a 14-day free trial, on the web, phones, Amazon Fire TV and Apple TV.

events.title: Criterion leaves Hulu
events.text: FilmStruck becomes the exclusive streaming home of the Criterion Collection.

events.title: “A terrible website”
events.text: The Verge praises the films and lists the faults of the site, including a Flash video player.

events.title: International plans
events.text: Turner International and Warner Bros. Digital Networks say FilmStruck will launch abroad, starting in Britain with the cinema chain Curzon.

events.title: FilmStruck Curzon opens in Britain
events.text: £5.99 a month, just over 160 titles, 34 of them from Criterion.

events.title: Warner Bros. classics arrive
events.text: More than 600 Warner Bros. films a month are added and Warner Archive’s streaming service is shut. The lineup grows to more than 1,800.

events.title: “If you love film, you’ll love FilmStruck”
events.text: Coleman Breland promotes the service at a Hollywood gala, six months to the day before its closure is announced.

events.title: France and Spain announced
events.text: With local partners including StudioCanal and MK2. Both launch in June.

events.title: AT&T completes the purchase
events.text: The merger closes at 5:57 p.m. Eastern. AT&T’s press release names FilmStruck among its new direct-to-consumer properties.

events.title: “Hours a day”
events.text: John Stankey, the new head of WarnerMedia, tells staff the company needs far more viewing time, as later quoted by the Los Angeles Times.

events.title: A new service, and how to pay for it
events.text: AT&T announces a streaming service for late 2019, to be funded partly by “consolidating resources from sub-scale D2C efforts.”

events.title: DramaFever closes
events.text: Warner Bros. Digital Networks shuts its Korean-drama service the same day it announces the closure.

events.title: FilmStruck’s closure is announced
events.text: Sign-ups stop at once; the last day will be November 29. Criterion says it is disappointed. A petition is started the same day.

events.title: 11,000 signatures
events.text: The petition has more than doubled in two days, Paste reports.

events.title: An estimate of 100,000
events.text: The Los Angeles Times refers to the service’s “estimated 100,000 subscribers.” No official figure is ever given.

events.title: 40,000 signatures
events.text: Barbra Streisand and Guillermo del Toro urge their followers to sign.

events.title: The letter to Toby Emmerich
events.text: Twenty-one filmmakers and actors send a letter to the chairman of Warner Bros. Pictures Group.

events.title: Deadline publishes two letters
events.text: The first is followed by a second with more than 30 further signers, including Sofia Coppola, Mira Nair and John Ridley.

events.title: “Something of a compromise”
events.text: Deadline reports that Stankey plans a new version of the idea inside the service due in late 2019.

events.title: The Criterion Channel will return
events.text: Criterion says it will relaunch its channel in spring 2019 as an independent service. Its post is dated November 15; the press reported it on Friday the 16th.

events.title: Last day of service
events.text: The U.S. and international services both cease.

events.title: The streams stop
events.text: At around 9 a.m., by one subscriber’s account.

events.title: A launch date for Criterion
events.text: April 8, 2019, in the United States and Canada, with lower prices for charter subscribers.

events.title: The Criterion Channel opens
events.text: More than 1,000 films at $10.99 a month.

events.title: HBO Max launches
events.text: WarnerMedia’s service arrives at $14.99 a month with TCM-curated classics and Criterion films.

events.title: A trademark lapses
events.text: The FILMSTRUCK registration covering streaming services is canceled. A second registration, for entertainment services, is kept.

events.title: Where things stand
events.text: filmstruck.com forwards to tcm.com. The petition shows 106,696 signatures.
